What Happened

Trump declared early this morning (Brasília time) that the conflict between the US and Iran could end without the need for a formal agreement with Tehran. He announced a national address for Wednesday evening, described as an "important update." Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the European Council President that Iran has "the necessary will to end this war," but demands guarantees against future aggression.

The news sparked a strong reaction in Asian markets: the MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose 4% in a single session, with Samsung and SK Hynix advancing over 9% each. S&P 500 futures also climbed. Brent crude, which had pulled back on Tuesday, stabilized again above US$ 105 after the Wall Street Journal reported that the United Arab Emirates is preparing to help militarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the first Gulf state to enter the conflict.

In the crypto market, ETH was the standout, rising 5.2% in the last 24 hours. BTC, meanwhile, remains within the same range of recent weeks, between $65k and $73k, reflecting a more cautious stance from investors toward the asset.

Why This Matters

The US-Iran war has been one of the main drags on markets since March. The prospect of it ending reduces the geopolitical risk premium that has been holding back the recovery of risk assets, including Bitcoin. Additionally, US Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows of
$1.32 billion in March
, the first positive monthly flows since October 2025, according to SoSoValue data. This indicates that institutional money is starting to return, albeit cautiously.
The Fear & Greed Index remains at
Extreme Fear (8)

, which shows that retail sentiment has not yet caught up with the price movement. In terms of derivatives, the BTC funding rate, which had been negative for days, approached zero this morning, suggesting that selling pressure via futures is decreasing.
